newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. rescinds approvals for three El Al routes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rescinds approvals for three El Al routes.

text.p: The United States has informed Israel and state airline El Al that it rescinded approval for three El Al routes between U.S. cities and Tel Aviv, Israeli aviation officials said Thursday.

The El Al routes include a twice-weekly flight from Baltimore-Washington, a weekly flight to Orlando, Fla., which was due to operate during the summer; and a route from Dallas-Fort Worth, El Al spokesman Nahman Klieman said.
The action was taken in response to a decision by Israeli authorities not to approve a New York-Athens-Tel Aviv route by New York-based Tower Air starting this summer, Klieman said.
He said Israel rejected the application because it had not been filed on time and told Tower it could begin the flights in October.
"We were surprised by the American decision. The transport minister will meet with the U.S. ambassador next week and we hope we can find a solution," said Transport Ministry spokesman Avner Ovadiah.
El Al had received permission to operate the Dallas-Fort Worth route but had not scheduled any flights, Klieman said.
He said El Al hoped the United States would reauthorize the routes once Tower's route had been cleared. "We will have to apply again and see what happens."
